I would step up surveillance. Another measure I would have taken was purely operative. I would have moved a unit like that, a unit that we didn't particularly trust, and put it somewhere else, along a different section of the front-line, to work alongside another unit that appeared to us more trustworthy, because had there been any enemy activity, the damage would have been limited.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gorjanc, imagine the following situation. You, as an HVO commander, lose control over a piece of territory, and then this area is conquered by the BH Army in cooperation with your own soldiers of Muslim ethnicity, and then all your misgivings are confirmed as a real and present danger. What would you, as a commander, do in a situation like that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN GORJANC
utterances.text: When I talked about surveillance measures, I would have applied those to all soldiers still remaining in my units. Wherever this danger was greater, especially near the front-line, I would have simply had no choice but to isolate those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gorjanc, let's look at what exactly happened, in territorial terms, following the 30th of June. Please look at 4D622. We're moving on to binder 3 right now, Your Honours, and this is the first document in binder 3. Mr. Gorjanc, since you're not a fact witness, everything we're talking about is hypothetical, of course. Assume that on the 30th of June the BH Army established control over a territory covering about 26 kilometres to the north of East Mostar, and assume that they established control over the territory stretching south of Mostar towards Buna and Blagaj. What would you say about that, about all these territorial conquests about East Mostar? Would you have considered that to be a militarily relevant development?

utterances.speaker: MILAN GORJANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In view of your knowledge and understanding of Bosnia and Herzegovina, if the road northbound is opened towards Jablanica and Central Bosnia, would, in such a situation, it be possible for the units of the 1st and 3rd Corps from Central Bosnia to come to fight in Mostar and further afield south?

utterances.speaker: MILAN GORJANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some documents that indicate that the services in charge of security --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a few minutes left only, and, Witness, this map for me is fundamental. Therefore, this deserves to spend a little time on it, a few minutes. According to this map, one can see that the HVO controls an area, including Mostar, part of it. In blue, we have the BiH -- sorry, in green, in green. In blue it's the HVO. In green, it is the BiH, and the BiH controls Mostar East, the east of Mostar. And then you have the Serbs, who are on the right of the document. Now, the question which, from my point of view, is very important, according to what you know, according to your knowledge, an inhabitant of Mostar East, can he, with this military map, leave Mostar East either by the north or by the south, inasmuch as one sees that the band is controlled by the BiH. The strip controlled by the BiH has a certain length. We don't have the exact length of the distance, but there are at least a few kilometres. So, I summarise, is it possible for an inhabitant of Mostar East to leave Mostar East, passing by the area controlled by the BiH, either by the north or by the south?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, he can pass. Now, we have on the left the HVO, and the Serbs on the right, according to this map. I suppose that the HVO had artillery, and I suppose that the Serbs also had artillery. Notwithstanding the fact that there was artillery on both sides, could an inhabitant of Mostar East, maybe by taking some precautions, leave by the north or leave by the south?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they could, especially during the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. With the technical knowledge you have, which is certainly 100 times superior to mine, could you -- can you tell me what is minimally the strip which is controlled by the BiH, as one sees it in the length or distance, as we see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In what sense? The width of the corridor, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the width of the corridor, the width.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The width of the corridor was some seven or eight kilometres. However, on the slopes of Mount Velez, it was impossible to take a route from the north to south, so this was limited to Donje Polje, the city of East Mostar, and the enlargement of Bijelo Polje, and further afield. In factual terms, it was possible to take several roads through the town, and then onwards towards Bijelo Polje there were just two roads, one along the River Neretva and the other one was the main road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. You are affirmative on this, you are positive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question before the end of the hearing, because there's another case coming. The inhabitants of East Mostar, since there could be some artillery shelling, was it easier during the night to take the roads towards the north and the south? Would it have been easier by night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was easier by night, when it comes to leaving the town and going towards the area of Buna and Bijelo Polje. It was, however, much more difficult across the mountain of Prenj in the direction of Jablanica, the western slopes of Prenj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's practically the time to finish our hearing, because I don't want to get in trouble with the Judges who are coming for the next hearing. We are, therefore, going to stop here. We will resume tomorrow. The Registrar will tell us how much time the Defence still has for General Petkovic. We will see this tomorrow. Apparently, we have to finish with one of the binders. Therefore, I wish everybody a pleasant day, end of the day, and tomorrow, sir, Witness, we will have the pleasure of seeing you tomorrow morning at the hearing, which will start at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
